text_fidelity_a:
bmanl Wireless Earbuds Bluetooth Headphones 48hrs Play Back Sport Earphones with LED Display Over-Ear Buds with Earhooks Built-in Mic Headset for Workout Purple BMANI-VEAT00L I purchased these to replace the Mpow Flame light that I had lost one of the earbuds too. I have gone through a couple of these.

What I do like is the charging case. It is pretty slim, it is USB C, and it also has a display to show how much of a charge it has. This is super helpful. It also has volume and connect/disconnect buttons. This has not yet had any charging issues, but I have not owned it for very long.

Now for what I don't like- They do not fit my ear that well. It may be the shape of hook, the length of the arm from which the speaker is mounted, or some other variable. The hook keeps it in place, but it never feels as if it's in my ear properly. I also think the sound is not so hot, and for 50 dollars I was expecting more. It is a little treble heavy on the heavier frequencies and just sounds like a cheap driver.

My previous headphone was the MPow Flame Lite. The charging case is bulkier and bare and there is no digital display. With that said- these are now 1/3 of the price. What I do like is that they fit my ear like a glove, and the sound quality is phenominal. It sounds like a much bigger driver. I am not an audiophile, but it really sounds great. Maybe it is the mid that come in fuller giving it a rich sound.

I have had some charging issues. Sometimes I find that only one of the headphones are dead and the other is fully charged. However, fit and sound are my most important details so these are my favorite. For the price I can purchase three and keep them in different places. If I lose one or have a charging issue I can replace it with the extra. This makes much more sense than keeping the aI do not more.

Edit: I changed from 3 to 5 stars. I have owned these now for almost one year, and use them probably every day. There has been no decrease in performance or battery life. I was so accustomed to my previous ear buds that I did not like these much at first. However, the sound is balanced, the battery life is great, and I really like the charging case. I have never actually times the batter life, but it is probably about 7-8 hours on a full charge. There are sooo many choices now for bluetooth ear buds, but these are a safe bet and most people should be happy. I am however not an audiophile, and someone who truly is may want to spend more on a Bose, or whatever the best ear buds are nowadays. My previous ones were more bass heavy, but these are better balanced. They do stay in the ear, unless I go to lay down on my back; I then have to push them back into my ear.
text_fidelity_b: bmanl Wireless Earbuds Bluetooth Headphones 48hrs Play Back Sport Earphones with LED Display Over-Ear Buds with Earhooks Built-in Mic Headset for Workout Purple BMANI-VEAT00L

text_fidelity_a:
GAOMON PD2200 130% sRGB Full-Laminated Pen Display with 8192 Battery-Free Tilt-Support Stylus 8 Touch Buttons -21.5'' Graphics Drawing Tablet Monitor with Adjustable Stand I am a huge supporter of open source graphics software because I feel that the leading brand name software uses their virtual monopoly to bully people into overpriced, restrictive, nonsensical subscription programs. When I saw that this tablet was listed as being compatible with GIMP and most other graphics programs, I felt comfortable purchasing it for my uses.

However, upon installing it, I found that it is not actually compatible with the vast majority of graphic software except for those supported by Adobe, and a couple of other inferior programs. To clarify, it will still "function" with most programs, but only as a basic mouse. It will not support pressure sensitivity nor tilt. This, in my mind, means that it is NOT compatible, as pressure and tilt are essential functions for any illustrator. Without them, this is basically just a glorified mouse pad.

From Gaomon's troubleshooting website regarding lack of pressure sensitivity:

"The version of your drawing program might be too low to support pen pressure. Please upload it or try to draw in other drawing programs. Here do we suggest you some drawing programs. For windows system: Adobe Photoshop CC, Adobe Photoshop CC 2015, Adobe Photoshop CC 2017, Adobe Photoshop CC 2018, Adobe Photoshop cs5，Adobe Photoshop cs6, Adobe Animate CC2017 For Mac system: Adobe Photoshop CC, Adobe Photoshop CC 2015, Adobe Photoshop CC 2017, Adobe Photoshop cs5, Adobe Photoshop cs6, Adobe illustrator cs6, Adobe Flash Professional CC, Adobe Animate CC 2018 Other free drawing programs: Sai, Krita, FireAlpaca"

Contrast that with the information in the product listing, which says, "compatible with most of major drawing software such as Photoshop、SAI version 2、Illustrator、krita、firealpaca、gimp、SketchBook Pro、MediBang Paint Pro, etc."

GIMP and others are clearly listed, but are not actually compatible. This is highly misleading.

As for other aspects of the tablet, I can't say too much as I haven't used it very much due to this issue. However, from what I have found so far, the display looks good, and the set up is pretty straightforward, although their manual is extremely confusing to try to follow.

The buttons on the side of the display are completely smooth and can not be felt; there is nothing there to help you locate them by tactile means, so you will have to stop looking at your work and visually find them in order to use them. They are also located such that they are easily pressed accidentally when adjusting the position of your tablet, which gets annoying pretty quickly.

The chords that come with the tablet are a bit short, maybe 4 or 5 feet, which doesn't allow for much room to position your tablet if you use a PC that is located beneath your desk or to the side, especially if the hook-up ports are on the back of the PC. You can of course buy replacement chords.

The stylus is very lightweight, which I personally consider a positive but some people may prefer a heftier stylus.

There is not much lag when using the stylus; the movement is smooth enough for my needs. The pressure sensitivity, when tested in a diagnostic program, seems quite good as well. It just doesn't work with the software I hoped to use it with.

Overall the tablet is a nice size and has a nice display, but the other issues are factors you should consider when deciding between this tablet and a more expensive brand.
text_fidelity_b: GAOMON PD2200 130% sRGB Full-Laminated Pen Display with 8192 Battery-Free Tilt-Support Stylus 8 Touch Buttons -21.5'' Graphics Drawing Tablet Monitor with Adjustable Stand

text_fidelity_a:
Dell Inspiron Gaming PC Desktop AMD Ryzen 7 2700 Processor, 16GB DRAM, 1TB HDD, AMD Radeon RX 580 4GB GDDR5 Graphics Card, Windows 10 64-bit, Blue LED, Model Number: i5676-A696Blu I benchmarked using 3DMark, Time spy. From the results you can see it falls about where you would expect for its hardware and pricepoint. You are going to do better than an entry level gaming laptop, but you aren't going to be blowing anyone out of the water. But... this comp isn't really made for high performance.

It did handle both Minecraft and Ark. If you have kids you may have run into issues with Minecraft being RAM greedy, which is why you want at least 8GB and this has 16GB. So it will handle it with most mods pretty well.

Ark is terrible on computers. Even high end gaming rigs can struggle with it. It is one of the reasons I used it for testing. It is so poorly optimized that it will crash your PC and chuckle at your demise. This computer handled it well on medium settings, which isn't too bad. I wouldn't run epic settings on anything short of a NASA computer, and even still I'd be worried it would crash the space station or accidentally launch missiles.

Bottomline; this computer will make most games playable, they will not be "epic". It's a decent entry level gaming computer. I am not going to tell you to build your own if you want to save money and get a better set up for the same amount. Honestly, if you were of the mindset to do that you would not be considering $700 Dell computers. I have built my own computer, I have also wanted to throw it on the lawn and light it on fire, because when something goes wrong I have no one to blame but myself, and no one to fix it either. So... ignore the "build it yourself" shamers. You do you. If you want to buy an entry level gaming computer go for it. I would strongly recommend saving up the additional $250 to get the upgraded version of this computer though. For not much more, you get a whole heck of a lot more computer. Better processor, better graphic card, way better storage, and an SSD to run your operating system.

I knocked a star for the price and because the driver update software they have on there is a joke. I had to go manually update drivers myself. If that's not your deal I recommend adding a 3rd party driver updater, do not rely on Dells. If you are feeling brave you can buy a more powerful gaming computer for $700, you will just have to do a bit more research that they are a legitimate company.
text_fidelity_b: Dell Inspiron Gaming PC Desktop AMD Ryzen 7 2700 Processor, 16GB DRAM, 1TB HDD, AMD Radeon RX 580 4GB GDDR5 Graphics Card, Windows 10 64-bit, Blue LED, Model Number: i5676-A696Blu

Logitech Wireless Anywhere Mouse MX for PC and Mac, black To be honest, I'm really tired of these mice failing.

They work great at first, then eventually quit scrolling or, worse, get stuck in scroll mode and drive the cursor to the bottom of the page for no reason. Two have failed on me. The first was purchased in 2011 for $36, the second in 2014 for $30. Both failed to scroll reliably and made using them impossible. Other, cheaper, wireless mice work better, or at least longer.

This mouse has nice features like left/right scrolling by tilting the scroll wheel and they work on many different surfaces, but those features fall by the wayside if the thing doesn't work at all after some time.

I've tried blowing it out with compressed air to clear debris, but it didn't fix it. Haven't come to taking it apart and cleaning it, as some proffer, because it's simply not worth the time.

For how much these mice cost -- $66 for the two -- they should be bulletproof. Better to buy cheaper wireless mice and throw them away when the fail.

I'm trying the $11 [[ASIN:B074DV98R7 VicTsing 2.4G Wireless Mouse Wireless Optical Laptop Mouse with USB Nano Receiver, 6 Buttons,5 Adjustable DPI Levels,15 Months Battery Life]] next. I could have purchased six of them for what I've put into Logitech MX Anywhere mice, both of which become landfill fodder.

Logitech has lost my Anywhere MX mouse business.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Wireless Anywhere Mouse MX for PC and Mac, black

text_fidelity_a:
Alphasonik ASE300BT Bluetooth Headphones, V4.0 Wireless Sport Headphones, Sweatproof Running Headset with Built in Mic for Workout Exercise IPX5 SplashProof, Ergonomically Designed for Extra Comfort I do a LOT of work in front of a computer, and was getting these for when I work at home. At work, I use a Logitech 930 headset that I really like. I got these so I wouldn't yank my laptop off the desk when I get up. I got bluetooth, thinking they'd be easy to sync to my various devices. So, here's my breakdown:

Range
I can go upstairs and grab a few things or go two rooms away and I still get a signal. The range is pretty good on these.

Playback Sound
The playback sound quality is okay. Not blowing me away, but alright. I listen to music, no vocals, to block out the office noise and keep my head focused. The playback audio goes into tin-can mode when the mic is enabled. That's something I didn't realize as a limitation of how bluetooth handles the two signals. That took me a while to figure out.

Microphone
The mic is okay. It just flips me out that the playback goes into "phone mode" when the mic is enabled.

Battery
Well, I've only had these a couple of months. But, the battery seems to go at least as long as I can stand to keep them on my head. Max has been about 2 hours at a stretch before giving my head/ears a break.

Fit
I'm an adult and my head is average-sized, not large. After maybe three months these cans are still a bit tight. The cups don't quite fit entirely over my ears and get uncomfortable after maybe two hours --like, *ouch* uncomfortable.

Heat
These cans get pretty hot after maybe 45 minutes. Hot like I just got out of the shower and I need a towel in my ears hot. I don't think I've ever had sweaty ears like this before from a set of headphones.

Sync
I've easily sync'd these to Ubuntu 14.04 & 10, Windows 7, and OS X Mavericks.

Would I recommend these to a friend?
No. I like not having to carry a dongle around since bluetooth is in all of my computers (one has an $8 dongle that works just fine.) But, they get so hot, and are still not comfortable on my head and ears after maybe 100 hours of use. So, for the $50 price tag, I'd probably have to say no. If they were $25 and just to make the occasional phone call I might recommend them to a friend, but not to wear for any period of time. If they were just a bit more comfortable, and breathed a bit better, I'd change my mind. Maybe in the next revision, Photive?
text_fidelity_b: Alphasonik ASE300BT Bluetooth Headphones, V4.0 Wireless Sport Headphones, Sweatproof Running Headset with Built in Mic for Workout Exercise IPX5 SplashProof, Ergonomically Designed for Extra Comfort

text_fidelity_a:
K&F Concept 49mm UV CPL Lens Filter Kit 18 Multi Layer Coatings Circular Polarizer Filter & MC UV Protection Filter Set for Camera Lens K-Series [[VIDEOID:2b8bb26ef242fcb874bd3c461ac0e558]] For the price, this is a decent circular polarizing filter for amateurs who want to get into using a polarizing filter. It includes a UV filter that I consider just an extra.

I personally don't recommend the use of UV filters unless you are shooting film, as they generally don't improve image quality on modern digital cameras and, if anything, can only degrade it. I know that a lot of people consider them a layer of protection for their expensive lenses, but I am of the opinion that having a cheap UV filter on your expensive lens is actually more likely to damage it. Case in point, the threads on this filter are very sharply cut. You can feel and hear them grinding when you screw it into place, and when it is tightened down snug, the sharp threads want to lock it into place. If the lens was knocked hard on the corner with the filter in this position, the UV filter might actually become stuck in place and damage the threads of the lens, requiring expert repairs to remove the filter and repair the lens. In my experience, just keeping the lens hood in place offers far more protection than a UV filter possibly could.

With that out of the way, let's get to the meat of this review, which is the CPL filter. For the price, this will perform perfectly well. It will darken the sky when used properly in the right conditions, and can help reduce glare and reflections. It seems to have no discernible color cast which would be a problem. In fact the only real issue I have with this filter is related to the mechanical function.

First of all, the threads are very sharply cut, as mentioned previously with the UV filter. This isn't the end of the world, but it is coupled by the fact that the rotating ring on the CPL filter is also very, very stiff and resists turning quite a lot. In order to turn it, as is necessary for adjusting it to the present conditions, you will need to tighten the filter down onto your lens more than I would like, and with such sharp threads, this increases the risk of the threads locking firmly onto your lens. It is possible for them to lock so firmly that it could be quite difficult to remove it from your lens. While $30 is a pretty good bargain for what is otherwise a pretty decent filter, it's not such a bargain if it runs the risk of costing you a lot of money in repairs to your expensive gear. If you are using a cheap lens, then this cheap filter should be just fine. If you have shelled out lots of money for an expensive lens, I would not recommend cheaping out on the filters.

In the end I settled on 4 stars because the glass is pretty decent quality, and if you are aware of the limitations you can safely use it so long as you avoid tightening it down too much. It's just a little less convenient. But it otherwise works well.
text_fidelity_b: K&F Concept 49mm UV CPL Lens Filter Kit 18 Multi Layer Coatings Circular Polarizer Filter & MC UV Protection Filter Set for Camera Lens K-Series

text_fidelity_a:
WAVLINK USB 3.0 Universal Docking Station with DVI/HDMI Dual Monitor Docking Station,2 USB 2.0 Port,2 USB 3.0 Port,Gigabit Ethernet,Quick Charging,Supports for Windows Mac OS The links on their site for the software download were not working, so I ended up having to go directly to DisplayPort to download the update. After that it was pretty smooth sailing.

I have kiddo all hooked up with dual monitors and his laptop docked and stored. So, now he has actual room at his desk to put his notebook or textbook or whatever else he needs for school, without the laptop taking up half his space.

To avoid any latency issues you can sometimes get while gaming and using DisplayPort software, I did hook his main monitor up directly to his laptop and "mirrored" the screen. This is the one he will play his games on. For his second monitor used for videos, research, etc. I used the HDMI port on the Wavlink dock and "extended" the screen. This way he can have dual monitors and bypass any latency issues that sometimes can crop up. If you can, it is also recommend when gaming to plug the mouse directly into the laptop as well, rather than the dock.

Personally, I don't notice any latency issues on either monitor or when the mouse is hooked up through the dock. But it was easy enough to just bypass the issue all together by how I plugged stuff in. The only struggles I had were with setting up his laptop to not go into hibernate instead of sleep after 2 hours, to stop disabling power to USBs while in sleep, and to allow his keyboard to wake the system out of sleep even though it was clearly already set up to do so. But that is nothing to do with the dock, and everything to do with Windows 10 being a pain in the behind sometimes. Finally everything is all set up, behaving as it should and we are ready for school to start next week. Well I'm ready, him... not so much.
text_fidelity_b: WAVLINK USB 3.0 Universal Docking Station with DVI/HDMI Dual Monitor Docking Station,2 USB 2.0 Port,2 USB 3.0 Port,Gigabit Ethernet,Quick Charging,Supports for Windows Mac OS

text_fidelity_a:
Lenovo IdeaPad 3 14" Laptop, 14.0" FHD 1920 x 1080 Display, AMD Ryzen 5 3500U Processor, 8GB DDR4 RAM, 256GB SSD, AMD Radeon Vega 8 Graphics, Narrow Bezel, Windows 10, 81W0003QUS, Abyss Blue I gave this to my daughter just over 5 months ago to use as her gaming computer (Minecraft, Fortnite, Among Us, Roblox). It worked BEAUTIFULLY for 5 months until one day out of nowhere, we, too, got the black screen of death that so many others have. It was still running, but the screen was black and my cursor had a spinning circle next to it. I am pretty good with computers so I tried all the usual fixes, and nothing worked. I’d always end up right back at the black screen.
BUT - I kept trying and I’m happy to report that I FIXED IT!!!

I opened a warranty claim with Lenovo & scheduled an appointment at Best Buy, but then after reading other reviews here, it was clear that this is a common problem. So I headed to YouTube. There’s a channel called PC Monkey & he has videos to walk you through all the troubleshooting for this problem. I tried all of the easy ones, but none worked. I ended up following his instructions for a fresh install of Windows from a USB - and lo and behold the laptop is like new again! It only took about 30 minutes to complete the process, and you will need another computer + a flash drive to download the install file.

I probably will not buy another Lenovo after this experience. I hope this review helps someone else who runs into the same problem.
text_fidelity_b: Lenovo IdeaPad 3 14" Laptop, 14.0" FHD 1920 x 1080 Display, AMD Ryzen 5 3500U Processor, 8GB DDR4 RAM, 256GB SSD, AMD Radeon Vega 8 Graphics, Narrow Bezel, Windows 10, 81W0003QUS, Abyss Blue

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin nüvi 360 3.5-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator with Text-To-Speech (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I've had this Nuvi 360 since Dec, 2006. It really works well. I carried it with me to DC. Even on foot it was terrific. It knew where all the restaurants and points of interest were and faithfully navigated us around the ancient horse paths of the Virginia/DC area. Believe me, when you pop out of an underground Metro station in the middle of the night and have no idea where you are or which direction to head off in, the ol' Garmin was there.

It's so small it easily fits in a pocket. The built-in battery lasts reasonably long. In the car, the 12-Volt adapter allows the unit to stay on indefinitely. You can select which accent and which gender you want the voice prompts to speak. Australian "Bruce," American "Jill" and a host of other combinations. All very fun. The voice prompts are the best. You really don't need to look at the thing while driving because it's uncanny in telling you what to do when you need to do it. It is amazingly accurate: something like 20 feet. It takes you right to the destination driveway.

It acquires the sats quickly and doesn't get flustered if you violate its recommendation and go in a different route. It just says, "recalculating" and finds another route for you. None of this "make a U-turn, bonehead!" It gives you enough time to make the turns, too. Also, it displays how far it is until the next turn. Very nice. No need to worry if you've missed it.

If you are planning on going to Europe, buy the unit that comes preloaded with both US and Europe maps as purchasing the Europe maps after the fact will really jump the cost unnecessarily.

I haven't used the Bluetooth capability yet but might later...after I get a Bluetooth phone.

The display is quite viewable in daylight and very bright at night, though it can be set to auto-dim at sundown so it's not too bright at night. You can touch the screen and scroll the map under your finger much like Google Maps can, to preview your route if desired. It shows coordinates and you can save them as destinations if desired, even if the location doesn't have an official street address. It is an MP3 player and can display photos and play Audible books on tape. When you are using the MP3 or Audible features, it pauses the file playing back to announce directions, then returns to the file without losing any of the MP3 file or book info. Very nice.

At extra cost, it has the ability to add foreign language dictionaries which can verbally speak phrases and words to you. You can also add Travel Guides and other software via the SD chip slot.

Overall, I'm very pleased with this device. It's accurate, fast, functional and small.

The one thing that doesn't work is the windshield suction mount. It broke before I even used it once. The plastic loops on the suction cup that receive the ball arm's hinge pin are too thin and fragile and broke with just a little normal hinge adjustment.

I recommend the model 010-10908-00 friction mount that looks like a bean bag with a ball arm sticking up. I made something similar by taking an unneeded 1/4" thick mousepad and epoxying a couple of small 1" x 1" angle brackets to the pad to hold the ball arm that I salvaged from the broken suction cup mount.

A friction mount is interchangeable with multiple vehicles, doesn't slide around on the dash and allows complete and rapid removal and/or hiding to avoid theft. Plus, you don't have to glue a disk to the dash for the suction cup to attach to.

UPDATE 10-22-07:
The 360 works well enough; better than most. It should: Five point three bills should deliver one heck of a map!

I've had it since Dec 2006...less than one year. Today I get an offer from Garmin to update my North American map software for a mere point seven bills. That's AFTER the five point three bills I already sunk into this little electronic gizmo.

I heard Garmin has a one year free map update policy, but their website won't let me do it. Not cool. The cost of the unit has already fallen significantly from what I originally paid and now they want more to get it current, within a year of purchase. Not cool at all. Also, impossible to contact by email. Garmin website is in a permanent loop back to itself when clicking on the "contact by email" option. Otherwise, it's call and wait on hold between certain times. Not cool again.

Then a friend says how well his Verizon GPS works on his wireless phone. I look into that. Verizon offers a full time GPS cost and a single use option for under three bucks per use.

For what I have wasted on this Garmin--over five bills and counting upward forever with their unfriendly updates--that's a whole heck of a lot of one-time Verizon uses with what will be the most updated, most accurate database. After all, no one's going to beat the phone company with accurate phone numbers and addresses.

If I hadn't already bought into the Garmin ripoff, I'd definitely go with Verizon's phone based GPS: the phone will always be with you when you need it instead of in the glove compartment in the other car.

And it most likely won't get stolen. It's a darned pain to have to put the Garmin away after each use so some cretin won't bash in a window to steal a very, very expensive toy that could just as easily fit inside a phone.

Go with the phone.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 360 3.5-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator with Text-To-Speech (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech G13 Programmable Gameboard with LCD Display Pros:
-Easily programmed.
-Multiple game memory.
-Many, many keys = many, many programming options.
-Digital readout looks good and lets you know exactly what download you are using without reopening Logitech window.

Cons:
-Flat palm positioning is not very comfortable for gaming (and can't be adjusted). My hand tends to cramp due to its bad ergonomics when playing FPS games more than an hour.
-Keypad ergonomics are badly thought out. Key rows are positioned bowing UPWARDS (away from your fingers) instead of downwards, making quick initiation of pinky and index finger keys more difficult.
-G13 is a bit large and can't easily be slid aside when not gaming (not a big deal to me, but somewhat inconvenient).
-Friends tell me that Razer and Logitech downloads interfere with one another, so if you have a Razer mouse or keyboard this may interfere with your use of either.
-Keys are a bit too close together without easily discernible gaps in between. This too often causes my thick fingers to strike 2 keys simultaneously.
-Overpriced for what it offers.

Overall:
Programming=excellent. Ergonomics=horrible.
For me, the keypad layout and palm rest do not work together. They look like they should, but they simply do not. The device concept is quite good, but the ergonomics make it just too difficult to consistently access and manipulate keys for real-time gaming. Very disappointing to me because with Logitech's years of experience in peripherals this should put Nostromo to shame---it simply doesn't because of the badly positioned keys and faulty wrist/palm rest ergonomics.

Follow-up:
-Down from 2 to only 1 Star, and it should be ZERO Stars. This thing is good only for a paperweight to remind me of my wasted time and wasted money.
-6 months down the road and, while gaming, each and every one of my gaming profiles (I have 3) will spontaneously reset to the default profile on their own or, even worse, all the G-keys become unresponsive.
-Sometimes on computer start-up the LCD screen lights up, but no profiles appear, not even default, and no keys respond.
-Sometimes on computer start-up the unit never powers on.
-Logitech's updates do not fix the problem(s). I've deleted the entire gaming software setup and performed reinstalls ad nauseum with no permanent positive result. What's even worse is this: it acts fine for a bit after a reinstall, so you think you've corrected it, then it starts screwing up ALL OVER AGAIN.
-BIOS adjustments do not fix the problems.
-USB ports and motherboard are completely functional throughout my gaming (I've tested/monitored them as I play) and they perform perfectly as the gamepad and/or its software crashes on its own.
-It's only 6 months old, and 2 keys are mechanically non-functional (G20 and the button below the joystick). My Belkin Nostromo n52 lasted for almost 8 YEARS of gaming with no problems whatsoever, and I was gaming three times as much back then. I'd grown used to the G13 so I was willing to overlook the buttons, or blame them on myself, and work around this issue, but when the software/electrical issues began occurring quite regularly I'd run out of patience.
-Forums addressing these (as well as other) issues have found no answers or solutions, only make-shift quick-fixes.
-Numerous forums also share the information that this is happening across a variety and multitude of different computer systems/set-ups.
-Many other owners, myself included, have had additional problems with the G13 when it is used after a computer has hibernated/slept, but we all learned to live with this as one of its quirks. We now see this as an indicator of its many issues.
-Many other owners have said that the problems began occurring after 3 or more months use (I suspect that in my case this took longer as it is only occasionally used for gaming).
-Logitech customer support has denied any fault in these matters and still maintains that their pruduct and programming is NOT the cause of any of these problems, so their help line has been useless. Meanwhile, the price plummets as word spreads.
-Only thing that works for any of us is to constantly disconnect gamepad from its current USB port, reconnect it, and computer may recognize it...but this does NOT always work...sometimes requires reboot as well...and sometimes this doesn't work either...so gamepad is inoperative until it decides to come back on a reconnection or restart. This is a band-aid at best. I refuse to do this to my system over and over.

This thing is getting returned. I advise you to save your money and time by buying some other manufacturer's product.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech G13 Programmable Gameboard with LCD Display

text_fidelity_a:
Sennheiser HD 598 Over-Ear Headphones - Ivory Recording my listening experience with the Sennheiser HD 598 which I bought after breaking my pair of HE-400 headphones. I own Grado Labs SR80, BModed Fostex T50, Sennheiser HD-600, Hifiman HE-500.

Hour 1:
Pro: Looks good for plastic and reasonably comfortable.
Con: heavy handed, muddy, base reminds me of a one-note subwoofer, and the signature reminds me of a cheap pair of Skullcandy headphones. You could get better sound from a pair of Beat headphones. I am feeling ripped off and don't recall the last time listening to music made me MAD!
One word: Garbage!

Hour 10:
The headphones have opened up some. Vocals feel recessed. Bass still feels one dimensional. Upgraded rating from one to two stars.

text_fidelity_a:
LENRUE Portable Wireless Bluetooth Speaker with Built-in-Mic,Handsfree Call,AUX Line,TF Card for iPhone Ipad Android Smartphone and More (Grey) I've been wanting my own bluetooth speaker forever. The interesting thing is that I'm not even interested in the bluetooth capability. I want the aux connection for my first generation iPod, which doesn't have bluetooth technology. My iPhone just doesn't have the space for all the music I have on the iPod, plus I don't want to use up data streaming Pandora. Additionally, bluetooth and getting stuff to connect is just a pain. So, I've never tried to connect via bluetooth only the aux.

At first I thought I had dud. I charged it and went to push the power button and nothing happened. I read the tiny print in the instructions and still nothing. So, I went on YouTube to see if anyone made video about using this and of course there is! So, you have to press the power button until the device glows blue and beeps! No where on the instructions does it say to do this! So, once you do this, then you can follow the directions to use the speaker. If you are going to just use the aux plug then push the "M" button, which I think stands for mode. You're good to go.

Now this is tiny, so you're going to get a lot of output, but it what it does put out is a decent sound. I have used mine in a small pavilion for a party and on my front porch. At the party depending on the song, a few downloaded from the early aughts were too quiet to hear, but songs downloaded from iTunes or from CDs came out loud enough to hear throughout the pavilion. Just make sure the volume is up on your speaker AND your device. I've used for about 12 hours total. 4 hours here, 4 hours there, etc., and I still haven't charged it. So it holds a good charge to last through a party or an afternoon lounging on the porch.

You get an aux cord and a USB charging cord. So you can charge it on the computer or with a charger plug that uses a USB plug. The light ring turns red when charging and goes off when it's fully charged. The ring glows blue when it is on. It flashes when it it searching or looking for a bluetooth device. I bought this after a family member refused to let me use his "expensive someone is going to steal it" bluetooth speaker even though he never uses it (and I'm never in a situation to have someone steal it.)
text_fidelity_b: LENRUE Portable Wireless Bluetooth Speaker with Built-in-Mic,Handsfree Call,AUX Line,TF Card for iPhone Ipad Android Smartphone and More (Grey)

text_fidelity_a:
Altec Lansing iM227 Orbit MP3 Speaker Overall, I'm pleased with this speaker. It hits the mark where it counts the most -- great sound. It makes the audio output of the Kindle Fire sound SO much better!

I also like that it runs on removable batteries. Many of the other small speakers I looked at had an internal rechargeable battery. While that has some advantages, the fact that the Fire does not have a USB port means I'd have to charge them from an outlet (with an adapter) or on my PC. Plus, non-removable batteries can present a problem when they fail. The Altec Lansing uses 3 AAA batteries which are far easier to deal with. I still use rechargeables (either Eneloops or the Amazon Basic rechargeable) and get several hours of play time per charge.

The shortcomings relate to the cord. It's short (about 8 inches) and is very thin. It would be a much better product with a longer cord (about 12 inches) and a cord that's made of more substantial material. I can see the cord being a potential point of failure down the road due to its lightweight construction.

But overall, it's a good device and a great value (if you catch it on a price dip). Highly recommend as an add-on to the Fire.
text_fidelity_b: Altec Lansing iM227 Orbit MP3 Speaker

Hooked the router back up and the DNS problems continued. I gave the router to a friend who is a network engineer for a works for a large IT services company to have him test it. He had the same DNS problems I had with it. So at least I know it wasn't anything I was doing wrong. Too bad I can't return it as it is after the return window. I Contacted Netgear support and they are giving me the runaround. Haven’t heard back from them in over a month. There are many many mentions of the same issue on the Netgear support forms. Basically their firmware update took a perfectly good router and turned it into a brick. Netgear support doesn’t have a solution and probably trying to just hold out long enough until I give up or the support window closes.

The XB33 was the perfect size to replace it, however the sound quality was below par.

The X55 had a wonderfully balanced sound with the woofer and two tweeters giving tight bass and crisp mids and highs. The xb33 with just two woofers has almost no mids and the highs are muddy at best. The xb33 DOES play much LOUDER then the x55, so for parties this would be the better choice. However, my needs are for low to mid volume while camping, so I tried the xb43.

The xb43, with two woofers and two tweeters has the balanced sound I wanted. The size sucks: The xb43 looks and feels much larger and is MUCH HEAVIER. (nothing is free)

I returned the xb33 and kept the xb43.

text_fidelity_a:
TCL 65" Class 4-Series 4K UHD HDR Roku 2017 Smart TV - 65S405 Do not be afraid! This is a great TV.

The good: I won't go into the technical details and explanations. Others have done that for me. We purchased this for a new home and have had it set up for a couple of weeks. The integration of Roku is seamless, and it retains those same intuitive menus. It has no WiFi connectivity issues for us (we have a Google mesh network with a good signal at the TV location), and effortlessly streams Netflix, Amazon Video and You TubeTV-- DVR and live-- and looks great doing it. I haven't tried 4K content yet, so can't comment on that.

The bad: It doesn't handle low light scenes very well in movies and television, and particularly when viewed from any angle that isn't straight on. That's why I gave it four stars instead of five. If you can overcome that, forge ahead! I couldn't justify spending twice or more on Samsung or others. Another minor quibble-- silver feet on a black frame looks a little odd.

The bottom line: I was skeptical. I've owned Samsung plasma and LED and an LG LED recently and I see no material difference between the TCL and the other LEDs. All the positive reviews here, plus the CNet reviews/primers on Roku integrated TVs put me over the edge. We really like this TV and it's simplified our streaming incredibly. Go get it!
text_fidelity_b: TCL 65" Class 4-Series 4K UHD HDR Roku 2017 Smart TV - 65S405

text_fidelity_a:
TOZO T6 True Wireless Earbuds Bluetooth 5.3 Headphones Touch Control with Wireless Charging Case IPX8 Waterproof Stereo Earphones in-Ear Built-in Mic Headset Premium Deep Bass White (2022 Upgraded) I just got the TOZO T6 waterproof headphones tonight. One of the main reasons I picked them is because they were same day delivery for me. Since my skullcandy wireless earbuds had ticked me off for the last time I was ready to find something new. I am so happy to say that so far I am not disappointed.

First of all, the packaging was immaculate. The unboxing experience felt like I was unboxing a new phone. Everything was packaged so neatly and purposefully.

Fit - There is a wider availability of earbud sizes than any other headphones I have ever gotten. Not just in girth, but also depth, so there is an option for people who may have a more shallow ear canal. Very thoughtful. As soon as I paired the earbuds and picked the appropriate sized silicone earbud tip I put them in. They were lighter and fit more ergonomically than my skullcandy did. They are smaller and fit my ear more comfortably.

Pairing - the process as simple as pulling the earbuds out of the box, taking the plastic tabs off, putting them in the charging case, taking them out of the charging case and waiting for the colored lights to begin flashing blue and red (took about 6 seconds). Then I scanned for TOZO 6 under "bluetooth settings" on my phone. It was literally the simplest pairing experience I've ever had. Especially considering I nearly returned my skullcandy earbuds after over an hour and them not showing up on my phone when I scanned. This was pleasantly simple and the directions given actually worked as they were supposed to.

The sound - I didn't do any adjustments to the sound on my phone, other than volume and the sound was crisp, it was full bodied, clearly hearing bass, and even the highest notes in clarity. I had the volume of the song I was listening to at a bit less than 50% and full sound that didn't allow normal room noises to infiltrate. I even knocked quite hard on my wooden nightstand to test this and I could not hear the knocking.

There is the option to alternate which earbud is first or secondary. Just turn off the one you want to be secondary and the other will remain primary when you turn the other back on again. I appreciate that either earbud can be primary or secondary or that can be used one at a time as well.

Phone call clarity. I was able to hear crisp clear sound while on the phone and the person I talked to said I sounded crisp and clear as well.

Charge - the earbud case is able to charge on a charging platform or with a micro-USB charging cable (included.) This was the only disappointment I encountered as I would have liked the T6 case to a accept the same USB C cable that my Galaxy Note phone uses. That is a minor thing that would not make me not want to use these earbuds.

There were several colors to choose from, black, white, light blue, mint green, purple and pink. I chose the light blue since it matches my current phone case. However, if ever after your purchase you tire of the color of your case, there are silicone charger cases available on Amazon for purchase specifically for the TOZO T6 charger case. This can allow your earbud case to be conveniently hooked to a bag or belt loop.

I cannot vouch for battery life yet, since I have only had them a couple of hours. I've had them in my ears for about 1.5 hours and they are still reading at 100%. So I am giving it 5⭐ for now.

Over all well worth the $39.99 I paid for these. I'm so happy with my purchase.
text_fidelity_b: TOZO T6 True Wireless Earbuds Bluetooth 5.3 Headphones Touch Control with Wireless Charging Case IPX8 Waterproof Stereo Earphones in-Ear Built-in Mic Headset Premium Deep Bass White (2022 Upgraded)

Jabra Evolve 75 UC Stereo Wireless Bluetooth Headset / Music Headphones Including Link 370 (U.S. Retail Packaging), Black Update:
After playing around and research I have found out that the bluetooth dongle is a separate device - called Jabra Link 370. With installation of the headset I also installed Jabra Direct suite. It apparently has Device Setting page, where one can choose between the dongle and the headset. The dongle settings have somewhat convoluted 'Wireless Range' option, which was - by default - set to VERY LOW (why?!) and after changing it to NORMAL, the signal seems to be much better and I experience no issues - so far... So, I'm boosting the score to 4 stars for now, penalizing Jabra with one star less to have set up VERY LOW as default settings (really?) and also not having any support on this issue. They had nothing about such transmission or poor signal quality issue in FAQs or their Support web pages - while the fix seems very, very simple and it should be there as one of the first FAQs.
-----------------
Original:
Got this set for about 2 weeks now in my open office space and the noise cancelling quality is amazing. Plus, great sound quality (I listen to a lot of music while working) until... it lasts... The sound drops out for a second to few seconds every 20-30 seconds, some sort of network overloading effect, humans sounding like robots, skips just like if you were getting our of range - while the dongle is about 2 feet from the headphones. This is the most irritating for music, but when it happens in the conference calls then it is no fun anymore...
The dongle is inserted in my docking station, but it doesn't matter, because I had the same issue when it was inserted directly into my Lenovo P50 ThinkPad. It also reproduces same errors when headset is connected directly to the laptop's Bluetooth, without the dongle.
For something that costs this much money, such flaw in the Bluetooth design is UNACCEPTABLE!

text_fidelity_a:
Ring Video Doorbell Pro – Upgraded, with added security features and a sleek design (existing doorbell wiring required) Great Addition to Home Security System

First I should say there is no 100% perfect home security system. That is why I have a home security “solution” that incorporates several different, but tied together systems. I have a full Lorex Camera System, Smart Things Hub and a wired alarm system. But even with all that there was something missing. If I wasn’t home, all of the other items were only good after the fact. Meaning I could see who was at my door, or in my house after I got back home. Sure I could set alerts on those other devices, but when your phone chirps 10 alerts per hour, it just becomes white noise. These other systems had so many false positives I ultimately turned them off.

Pros: But the Ring Bell filled several voids in these other systems. One, the false positives are almost nonexistent due to the ability to mask the alert area of the camera. My existing security system may alert me, but then I had to log into the camera system to see what was going on. The time it takes to do that could make a real difference. The ability to answer and interact with someone who rings your bell from your couch or from at work is invaluable! The person ringing the bell has no idea where you are answering from. But the best part is being able to ignore solicitors and screen people before you answer. It’s as easy as answering a phone call and the live image is instantaneous. The fact that it integrates with my SmartThings hub is just icing on the cake.

I was able to install the Ring Bell Pro in about 15 minutes following the simple instructions. It is extremely well thought out. The video quality of the Ring Pro is excellent! It does not have a very wide angle and there is a slight fisheye distortion, but it should be more than sufficient for most applications. The mobile app is also very intuitive. As I mentioned, when you get an alert, you can immediately see who is at the door and you can choose to answer and speak, or just watch.

Cons: I was confused by the wall plate not having the mounting holes line up with the existing wall plate holes. This required drilling holes above and below the existing holes to mount the plate. I could see no reason for this.

The unit can easily be ripped off the wall with one hand. Because the main unit mounts onto a plastic wall cover, it would take about 2 seconds to remove and disable the unit. But at least you will get an alert and when you went to log in you would know something was wrong. However, the Ring Pro has a unique purchase protection that sates “If your Ring™ Video Doorbell is stolen at any time after your purchase, Bot Home Automation, Inc. will replace your Ring™ Video Doorbell at no charge to you”. That’s pretty impressive!

If you want to keep your Ring History, you have to sign up for their paid service. Otherwise you only see live views. Prices vary by plan, but they do offer one free month for new customers.

Overall: There is no perfect security system. Each one has its plusses and minuses. But the Ring Pro should be part of every home security solution. Also, if I had to choose only one component for a complete home security solution, this would be high up on my list.

Update: 7/10/2017 - The unit has powered down several times and gone off line. This has required disconnecting it at the unit or the bell inside and reconnecting it. I have verified my power supply works OK. We will see if this becomes a ongoing issue.

Update: 10/30/2017 - I have downgraded from 5 to 3 starts today. First, the unit still stops working at times and needs to be rebooted by disconnecting the wires at the bell. The existing analog bell only chimes for the Ding and not the Dong. However the biggest disappointment is a inherent design flaw in the phone application. If someone come to the door and quickly goes away, like the UPS guy, by the time you take out your phone, open the app and connect, they are long gone. So you do get alerted, but there is no way to access the app fast enough to get a live view of what happened. You have to wait a few minutes until you can review the past activity, which requires a subscription. I guess it's still better than nothing.
text_fidelity_b: Ring Video Doorbell Pro – Upgraded, with added security features and a sleek design (existing doorbell wiring required)

text_fidelity_a:
Onkyo HT-S3500 660 Watt 5.1-Channel Home Theater Speaker/Receiver Package This system ROCKS! We got it for our Roku, and aside from a few slight annoyances with the setup, it works and sounds awesome. It works very well for our living room and my wife can now hear the movies instead of asking me what they said all the time. I would like to point out for some people that the HDMI output to the TV is only for the HDMI inputs and not "One port to rule them all". If you use a component device with the red, blue and green plugs (us: older DVD player) you need to have a set run from component out to the component in on the TV. Same goes with the RCA style (red, yellow, white) to get video on that. I was very disappointed that I couldn't just run one HDMI to the TV and be done with it.

Secondly the unit gets warm. I mean very warm and electronic smelly. I read the other reviews and I also experienced a similar issue. So after a week, I grabbed an unused 120mm computer fan and a old router power supply and made a cooling fan that rests on the top of the head unit. It helped a ton. I no longer smell anything, and the whole thing is now cool to the tough. I control the power to the fan using one of those green power strips that turns off stuff. Others used a USB fan from the iPod port on the unit. I do recommend that you cool this somehow to increase its lifespan.

The speaker wire that came with the system is junk and too short for my purposes. I ordered some thicker gauge wire [[ASIN:B0029HHIDY RCA AH16100SN 100 Ft. 16-Gauge Speaker Wire]]for my needs. The sounds is great with this better/bigger wire and I could put it where I wanted.

So these maybe deal breakers for some, but the price was right and we live with the other issues, but since this unit works so well, it seems like a small price to pay for good sound. Overall I highly recommend this unit.
text_fidelity_b: Onkyo HT-S3500 660 Watt 5.1-Channel Home Theater Speaker/Receiver Package

text_fidelity_a:
Roku Express - HD Streaming Player It may not be a techie's delight, but if you are looking for a budget streaming device, this one fits the bill. First off it is quite small making it ideal for cramped or limited spaces like a vacation home or boat. It comes with a short, two foot long cable and a piece of two sided tape. It connects to your tv with the cable.Depending where you tv is located you might have to use a longer cable. I did and found that the tape is not just a nice idea, it is a necessity. the box is so small and most cables so rigid it flips the box off making it impossible to regulate with the infrared remote. Take time to position because while the tape adheres well it looses its stickiness after being removed and repositioned. The infrared remote must be in line of sight for it to work. The way around that is to use the app. The app works with both android and iOS. The app has a voice control which I found to be inconsistent and a private listening feature that lets you use your phone headphones and mute the TV.

Performance is mixed. navigating and launching is slow. Netflix in particular really dragged. but playing content was excellent with no lag or problems. the channel selection is good with pretty much everything you would want available.

This is not bad for a budget streamer. there are definitely downsides, the ir remote, the lack of speed, the need for a cable. but it does work and is small enough for travel. I am frequently on the road for business and this does expand the limited options of hotel televisions. If you are on a budget and don't need or want the features that are available on pricier models this low end streamer will get the job done.
text_fidelity_b: Roku Express - HD Streaming Player

text_fidelity_a:
ASUS WiFi Gaming Router (RT-AC5300) - Tri-Band Gigabit Wireless Internet Router, Gaming & Streaming, AiMesh Compatible, Included Lifetime Internet Security, Adaptive QoS, Parental Control, MU-MIMO i need to use this router longer and under different circumstances to be sure, but so far i'm not as impressed with it as i anticipated; so far i haven't seen it massively outperforming the third- or so generation dual-band 802.11n AirPort Extreme it replaced. it does outperform it; just not massively. i'm definitely not seeing the crazy long ranges people are referring to...down the block...half a mile away...all that nonsense. i go out into my driveway, putting one wall (part of which is window) and about 25 feet between my iPhone 6S Plus and this router and the signal starts to fall off; walk the 50 or so feet to my mailbox and the signal's down to that tiny little dot at the very bottom of the wifi icon. i'm sure if i went another ten feet i'd lose the signal altogether (and this situation remains the same whether i'm using tri-band SmartConnect, dual-band SmartConnect, or none). the signal seems to be great inside the house, but this house is tiny - it's a cottage - so that's not saying much.

and while it doesn't technically matter and is certainly not reflected in my rating, i just don't like the looks of the thing. it looks cold and evil. i was going to say "like Darth Vader sitting on my desk", but i never thought Darth Vader looked this...unsettling.

that's just my psychology though, and, as i say, of no actual consequence.

four stars because it does perform marginally better than the router it replaced, and the web interface is both fairly easy to use and gives much more control than AirPort Utility does.

what i wish i knew, and have looked for online to no avail, is how to optimize the myriad settings to be sure i'm getting the best performance this unit has to offer. i spent $400.00 on a router expecting great things and i'd like to get them if at all possible, and i don't know how, or whether i am. and a downside of having such extensive control over the router's settings (while not knowing how to optimize them) is that there are surely a lot more ways to run it at less than its full capability than there are to get the best out of it. can anybody point me to a good step-by-step guide on how to maximize this router's performance?
text_fidelity_b: ASUS WiFi Gaming Router (RT-AC5300) - Tri-Band Gigabit Wireless Internet Router, Gaming & Streaming, AiMesh Compatible, Included Lifetime Internet Security, Adaptive QoS, Parental Control, MU-MIMO

Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st) When my husband recently purchased a [[ASIN:B0071N6AC6 netbook]], he wasn't using his Kindle Fire nearly as much, and I inherited it. I had recently dumped my cable TV service in favor of using the Fire to watch online the few news and TV dramas that I normally had used my TiVo to record. I found that my Internet connection through a wifi router has a really hard time playing videos via the Fire. It would often lose connectivity or freeze up when my iPhone was working fine using the same connection, playing the same shows.

The Fire has a gorgeous interface, though, for reading eBooks compared to my Kindle Keyboard. However, I've been using a Kindle app so frequently the past few months on my iPhone, that both the Kindle Keyboard and the Kindle Fire feel too cumbersome to bother with most of the time in comparison as an eReader.

For searching the Internet, the Fire has an easier interface than the iPhone, so I use it more often for that, unless I don't have it with me--I always have my iPhone with me.

I don't use the Fire for MP3. It is just too huge compared to my tiny MP3 player.

I don't have magazine subscriptions in electronic form, so I don't use it for that, though I know I could if I wanted to.

I understand the Fire can support PDF, but I haven't used it for that yet.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st)

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Oasis – With 7” display and page turn buttons- Ad-Supported + 3 Months Free Kindle Unlimited (with auto-renewal) [[VIDEOID:a23b5cd930e819bd2cae7872ede2dd37]] I decided to finally upgrade my Kindle from the first Paperwhite when I found out I could get a 25% discount and a $5 Amazon gift card for trading in my very old and unused Kindle Keyboard 1st gen, as well as other bonuses of 6 months free Kindle Unlimited (approx $60) plus a 30 day Audible trial.

I’m very happy with it and it has some great features.
I do like the adjustable amber tint, but I also really like the ability to invert the colors to white print on a black background. This is even easier on the eyes, but it does have a noticeable (and irritating) white flash every few page turns when using the buttons, and almost with every page turn when advancing with the touch screen. I believe this is the e-ink refreshing. I will probably use the black inverted color only when I’m reading outside in bright sunlight.

I also am really happy to have buttons to turn the page again. It’s the ultimate laziness to be able to just keep your thumb in the button and depress it to turn the page instead of having to actually move your thumb a half inch to touch the screen, but hey, why move a half inch when your can push down 1/16th of an inch? All that extra movement add up over the years.
The real reason I like the buttons is this: I live in Alaska and we have very long, cold nights. But even in the winter, we turn down the heat at night. I read in bed every single night, tucked all cozy and warm under my down comforter... except for having to have my hand out in order to touch the screen on my Paperwhite to turn the page. My hand starts to get very cold. It’s uncomfortable. My half frozen hand takes away from my happy bedtime reading experience. With the Oasis, I can keep my hand under the blankets and just push the button. You don’t know what a big deal this is until you spend night after night with a frozen hand.

I also like that you can select which button to the the page advance button and which is the page back button. The Oasis comes set up with the top button as the page advance and the bottom as the page back, but I switched them: the bottom is the advance, the top is the back. I hold my ereaders at the bottom sides, and had to stretch my thumb to advance the page when it was set for the top button. It’s just easier and more comfortable to use the bottom button. And this is cool: the bottom button stays as my page advance button even when I rotate the Oasis 180 to use left handed!! Smart!!

Others have covered the size and weight so I won’t go it I all that except to say it’s comfortable to hold. I do use the official Amazon Premium leather cover and it fits perfectly, and the magnetic closure/sleep/wake functions work perfectly also.

Dislike: Nothing with the ereader itself, but with however Amazon picks the “special offers”. From what I read, these offers are supposed to be tailored off of a person’s reading history/preferences. I may be wrong.
The books they are featuring for me are “romance” genre. I am sooo not a romance genre girl. I don’t believe I’ve ever purchased this genre in my life. I’m a hardcore sci-fi/dystopian. I have an adverse reaction when I see romance special offer.

Other than that, some of the complaints by others leaves me wondering.
I just don’t think it’s THAT big of deal that it has a micro usb. Really, it’s just not that hard to figure out the big end of the cable from the small end. As for charging speed, charge mine while I’m sleeping at night so it doesn’t matter if it takes 1 hour or 4. I suppose having to carry a micro usb cord and charger when other devices use a usb-c cord/charger may be annoying but I think I can find 2 square inches in my purse/pocket/bag/backpack for it.

Also remember that this is an e-reader. It’s not a tablet, computer or smartphone, nor does it make any claims to be. Expecting an ereader to function basically like a computer/tablet/smartphone is expecting too much. It does an outstanding job at doing it’s job as an ereader.

I have sent many different type of files to my Paperwhite using my kindle email address and it’s worked excellent with that old ereader, so I expect this new Oasis will do excellent with those as well.

My suggestion is to read the description fully and know what you are getting and what you aren’t.
If your reading experience will be destroyed because this doesn’t have (nor claim to have) a usb-c, then this isn’t the ereader for you.
If you want it to be like a tablet or smartphone or computer, this isn’t the ereader for you.

But if you love reading and buy this for what it’s made for, I can recommend it.
Definitely look into getting a discount by trading in any unused kindles, and take advantage of the free Kindle Unlimited and Audible while they are available to offset the cost even more.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Oasis – With 7” display and page turn buttons- Ad-Supported + 3 Months Free Kindle Unlimited (with auto-renewal)

text_fidelity_a: Belkin 6-Outlet Pivot-Plug Surge Protector w/ Wall Mount - Ideal for Mobile Devices, Personal Electronics, Small Appliances and More (1,080 Joules) - (Pack of 5) My husband and I purchased this surge protector for our kitchen, where it lives just above my built-in desk.  We needed something that would permanently house the plugs for our cordless phone and answering machine yet also be available for recharging our cell phones, iPod, and my netbook computer.  This unit has served our purpose well.  The six plugs are spaced far enough apart to accommodate most larger transformer plugs without difficult; the fact that each plug swivels from the front to the side makes it even easier to arrange your devices as needed.  The only downside that I have found to this product is that it does feel slightly unstable:  there is only a single screw which connects the unit to the wall outlet, and so it does wobble a bit.  However, I have not found this to be a major problem; I have simply gotten into the habit of stabilizing the unit with one hand as I put the plug in or out with the other.  Overall, I would give this surge protector a rating of 4 1/2 stars, and I would definitely recommend it.

text_fidelity_a:
Microsoft Sculpt Ergonomic Wireless Desktop Keyboard and Mouse - Black. Wireless , Comfortable, Ergonomic Keyboard and Mouse Combo with Split Design and Palm Rest. I'm a huge fan of Microsoft keyboards. Never been much of a fan of their office productivity software, but when it comes to keyboards, Microsoft fits my needs to a T. I'm using the Microsoft Digital Media Pro keyboard which (I believe) was discontinued years ago. A shame, since it has so many useful features.

But out with the old and in with the new. I tried and did not care for the previous generation of ergonomic split keyboards from Microsoft. At first glance the Sculpt looked to be a better design. The divide between the two sets of keys did not appear to be as pronounced, and my hands seemed to fit the keyboard very well. Love the feel of the pad on the wrist rest area!

Installation was straightforward, although getting the items out of the box was a challenge. I was happy to see that the necessary batteries were included - nothing worse than having to go hunt for batteries before you can start to use a new device.

The keyboard feel strongly reminded me of a laptop. For some, that may be a good feature. For me it is not. The flat keys and shorter throw makes typing feel "unnatural." I know that sounds vague, but it's the best way I can describe it.

This odd feel translated itself into a much slower typing speed - cut my throughput by about half. Since I write reports for a living, that's a rather big issue.

I also could not come to grips with the function key placement, size and meager supply of ancillary keys. That's a feature I love with my current Media Pro keyboard in that I can map pretty much any of the ample number of multimedia keys to any function I choose, or even a URL. For example, to start SPSS, Excel and WP I press one key. Another single keypress also opens my browser and my Amazon cart URL (and yes, the lettering on that particular key is pretty much worn completely off from use).

Still, if I was forced to, I could live with the keyboard. I could not, under any circumstances, live with the mouse in this set. Feels poor, lacks refinement, and far less versatile than my Logitech M500. I tried my best to get used to the Sculpt mouse, but just grew to hate it the longer I used it.

Now, my opinions are certainly affected by my current choices in keyboards and mice since I've been using them for years and years. I've changed PCs at least three times, but have retained the same keyboard and mouse since they have worked so well. If you have less keyboard/mouse "muscle memory" perhaps the Sculpt will fit the bill. The build quality seems decent, and if they are as reliable as other Microsoft keyboards, it will continue to work for some time. But for me, I just can't move the approval meter past "meh" for the keyboard and "dud" for the mouse. Three stars.
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft Sculpt Ergonomic Wireless Desktop Keyboard and Mouse - Black. Wireless , Comfortable, Ergonomic Keyboard and Mouse Combo with Split Design and Palm Rest.

text_fidelity_a:
Sony HDR-PJ380/W High Definition Handycam Camcorder with 3.0-Inch LCD (White) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) While I'm quite comfortable using an SLR, I've not been all that handy with a camcorder in the past. It's been a few years since I used one, so I was curious to see if user-friendliness has kept pace with technological advancements.

With this model it has. I found it very easy to use right out of the box with just some minor trial and error. I did end up reading the manual (which is pretty decent) but the main functions were pretty self apparent by just fiddling around with it a bit. The menu structure is logical and well presented; the screen is clear and easy to view.

The overall build quality is excellent. It feels more substantial in hand than I expected at this price point while retaining a very lightweight and easy to carry profile. I like the button placement - feels very natural in hand.

I love having the internal memory for storage as well as the little touches, such as a built-in USB connector. These features help make this a grab-and-go type of device, which increases the likelihood and ease of bringing it along and capturing video. (Note: you can also use a plug-in memory card should you want to.)

The video quality in good light/outdoors is excellent - very sharp and clear. Low-light performance is a somewhat grainy but quite decent. Stills are pretty decent. It won't put an SLR to shame, but it's more than good enough for casual snapshots. The internal mic works well and is more immune to wind noise than I expected.

My only significant disappointment with the cam is the projector. Wonderful idea, but the actual performance is lackluster. The projected video is hard to see clearly if there's any appreciable amount of light in the room. The 100 inch projection spec is wildly optimistic if you expect to actually see what is being projected.

Given that this cam does everything else so well, is so easy to use, and a breeze to tote along, I won't detract any stars due to the shortcomings of the projector feature. This is a great cam for the novice cam user (such as myself) or even an intermediate user. However, if the projection feature is a primary need, this may not be a good cam for your needs.
text_fidelity_b: Sony HDR-PJ380/W High Definition Handycam Camcorder with 3.0-Inch LCD (White) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
THINKWARE F550 Full HD Dash Cam with high-speed Cortex A8 Processor, GPS Tracker & Dual Save Technology I've tried some low-cost in-car cams and have been unimpressed with the build quality or video quality of the devices. The Thinkware 550 was a marked departure - it feels very well-built and solid. I'd rate the build quality up there with a decent conventional camcorder, such as a Sony. It also looks very attractive - they did a great job with the design.

This is not an "action cam" type of device for uploading videos of during stupid stuff onto Youtube (sorry, showing my age here - I probably would have done the same had cams been around in my youth). Rather, it's a cam for automatically documenting events that occur while driving (such as a crash or other incident) without any need for user action. Video files are time and date stamped, and assigned a location using GPS. It's more of a "black box" type recording device for a car rather than a "fun time" action cam with a car mount.

You can also use this while parked and with a rear camera, but both of those require additional items not included with this package (hard wire install for parking use; a separate camera for rear view use).

Installation is easy but also a little bit tricky. The mount is a plastic cradle with an adhesive backing. Once you determine where you want the cam mounted (up on the windshield is the recommended position) you peel off the backing on the adhesive pad and stick it to the windshield. It's a permanent mount (well, you can remove it from the glass, but it can't be reused). Easy to do, but tricky in that you really need to take some time before committing to a location and think through where the power cord needs to be routed.

The unit is lightweight (5.1 ounces without the cradle) and seems to be holding well to the windshield even over very bumpy terrain.. The manual suggests leaving the cam off the cradle until the adhesive has cured for 24 hours. I didn't see that tip until after I tested its holding ability over broken road. So if you miss that tip as well, it doesn't seem to be a problem.

The cam does not have a built-in battery. It must be powered by an included cigarette lighter adapter (known by "power ports" these days, but I still call them cigarette lighters). The adapter is very nicely made with a stout cord. That's good for longevity; not so good for routing it so the cord is not visible or in the way. There are some adhesive tabs included to lasso down the cable to help make for a neat (or semi-neat) install. I'll probably add some electrical tape to neaten up the install a bit more.

The manufacturer also cautions to make sure the power port you use gets shut off when you turn off the engine. The cam can continue to pull power if the power port is live, potentially draining your car's battery.

It automatically powers up when you start the car. It can be manually turned off (or back on) as well. It offers two recording modes: continuous (which is in one minute segments) or on-demand (you can manually start and stop). It also states that when there is an impact, the cam will store the 10 seconds before and the 10 seconds after in a secure memory folder. I'll have to take their word for that - can't really test that out! Under normal circumstances, when the micro SD card fills up it starts overwriting old files.

A micro SD card is included along with a reader. The card holds the user manual and the software, so it can't really be used to store video files. I used my own card reader rather than the one included since the included one was too tiny for my clumsy fingers to deal with.

There is no viewer on the cam - you have to take out the SD card and pull up the files using the included software. That for me is the biggest problem and limitation of this device. You have to trust that it's working since there's no confirmation other than the indicator lights and prompts. Nor can you set the camera specs unless you have access to a PC.

On the plus side, the lack of a screen means there's no risk of driver distraction while the cam is operating. I can't fault that. Still, I would have liked to see a design that has a screen that remains off until the camera is out of the mount so it can be used in-car to change settings or review stored video. That maintains the lack of driver distraction but still allows for better use of the cam while parked.

What makes up for a lot of these shortfalls is the video quality. Great - really great. Crisp, clear and sharp. It provides a panoramic view (the specs say 140 degrees) that easily covers the full view from the windshield. You really won't believe this is from a car cam. It dealt with head-on full sunlight pretty well, and did a decent job at night. I did get a fair amount of reflection off the windshield at night, but the video was very workable.

The included software installed fine on a Win 7 machine after I suspended Avast from running - this software does not want to work and play well with Avast. I even had to keep Avast suspended while running the software. Not tough to use - got the hang of it from just trying out menu options and playing around. It will ask to install an update right off the bat.

The video quality and overall "forget about it and it just records" type of operation are strong pluses. The power cord, mounting system, and lack of a view screen are problems. Weighing everything together gets me to a 3.5 star rating which I'll round up to 4 stars since the video quality is so nice. If you can live with the limitations, this is well worth considering.
text_fidelity_b: THINKWARE F550 Full HD Dash Cam with high-speed Cortex A8 Processor, GPS Tracker & Dual Save Technology

text_fidelity_a:
KINESIS Freestyle2 Ergonomic Keyboard w/ VIP3 Lifters for Mac (9" Separation) UPDATE 1/5/14: I'm downgrading my rating of this keyboard to three stars for one main reason: there are very sharp edges on the inside of the two sides of this split keyboard which can cut your wrists if you aren't careful. I put my mouse in between the two sides of the keyboard because that is the best position for it for me to prevent back and arm strain. Unfortunately, every time I use the mouse, my right wrist runs into the sharp edges of the inside of the right side of this split keyboard. To give you an idea how bad this sharpness is, I wear a [[ASIN:B008C27UPQ sport wristband]] to protect my wrist, and it is literally shredding from coming in contact with the knife-sharp plastic edge. I have tried putting duct tape over the sharp edge, but it won't stick to the plastic this keyboard is made of, and to add insult to injury, the tape looks awful.

Previous Review:

I recently had a bad flare-up of right arm pain from repetitive stress. I experimented to figure out which movements at my computer were hurting me the most, and I realized that reaching for the mouse was even more painful than keyboarding. As a result, I searched for keyboards here on Amazon with the potential to be divided in half, so that I could place my mouse right in front of me. That search led me to this keyboard.

This "freestyle" keyboard gives you the option to either leave the two sides hooked together and place it at a 45-degree angle on each side, or unhook the two sides totally. It is a simple procedure, no tools required, to unhook the two sides.

This product comes with instructions for putting the keyboard together from scratch, but everything came assembled except for mounting the padding that supposedly goes under your wrists--I have medium-sized hands, and the padding lands at the base of my hands, nowhere near my wrists. The padding also is not very thick, and I'm not sure why the manufacturer did not just go ahead and paste on the padding themselves--it's a hassle making sure it is totally straight before you stick it on. It can't be re-positioned if you mess up. Fortunately, I didn't mess up, and I don't have a huge need to support my wrists, so I am not downgrading my rating for that, but some consumers might want to know about it.

I really like the ability to put my mouse pad in between the two halves. This works as well as I had hoped to prevent the strain of reaching for the mouse constantly. The keys have a nice feel to them, as well. I am a touch typist, and I was very concerned at first that I would lose that ability on a strange keyboard. I have learned after multiple long days of using the keyboard that the trick is to get my fingers in the right position to begin with, such that my right pointer finger is on the J, and my left pointer finger is on the F. Even so, I currently hit false keys much more than normal. I hope that time and use will overcome this issue. I have ordered an additional one of these keyboards to hook up to my laptop so that I am always employing the same keyboarding reflexes, in order to more quickly retrain my brain.

This keyboard is certainly much more expensive than the $15-19 keyboards I've used forever, but will be well worth the price if it, as I think it will, helps prevent the excruciating pain of repetitive stress syndrome.

This keyboard is made so that the inner section can be elevated at either of two selected heights, or it can be fairly flat. This is useful for varying the position of the hands. As a physical therapist told me years ago, changing position and resting are crucial for preventing repetitive stress. I've tried all three levels, and I find the highest one the most comfortable.

Another plus of this keyboard is that I can now bilaterally employ a beneficial PT suggestion: I have for years placed a pillow under my right arm which is positioned against the arm of my [[ASIN:B000PWGZOI rolling office chair]]. This takes the strain off my arm and shoulder by bracing them. The fact that I'm using a pillow means that I am not in danger of damaging the brachial plexus nerve in the axilla (underarm), which can happen with hard objects like crutches. Previously, it never felt comfortable when I used a traditional keyboard to do this for my left arm, but with this keyboard, it does. Now, with both arms/shoulders braced, I find that it is much easier and even automatic to keep my back straight and my head up. It has greatly eased not just arm and hand strain, but back, shoulders and neck strain as well. In addition, I make a point to take my hands completely off the keyboard and mouse when reading, vs. keyboarding, and the pillows give me a comfortable place to elevate my hands, on the top of the pillow where it extends from beneath my underarm.

I rate this product as follows:
Ease of use: 4 stars (should improve with practice)
Functionality for preventing muscle strain: 5 stars
Comfort of use on wrist: 3 stars
Ease of assembly: 4 stars
Attractiveness of keyboard: 4 stars
text_fidelity_b: KINESIS Freestyle2 Ergonomic Keyboard w/ VIP3 Lifters for Mac (9" Separation)
